informal_statement: Hilbert.KTB is strictly weaker than Hilbert.S5.
informal_proof: Hilbert.S5 is a modal logic that includes the axioms of Hilbert.KTB along with additional axioms, such as the McKinsey axiom (□(□p → p)), which allows it to prove a broader range of theorems. Specifically, while both systems deal with necessity and possibility, Hilbert.S5 incorporates additional rules and axioms that Hilbert.KTB does not, rendering it more expressive and powerful. This can be demonstrated by constructing a Kripke model where a formula is valid in Hilbert.S5 but not in Hilbert.KTB, thereby establishing that Hilbert.KTB is strictly weaker.

informal_proof:
We aim to demonstrate that the Hilbert system KTB is weaker than Hilbert system S5, denoted as Hilbert.KTB ≤ₛ Hilbert.S5. This involves showing that every theorem provable in KTB is also provable in S5.

To establish this, we consider the frame classes associated with these Hilbert systems. Hilbert.KTB corresponds to the frame class `ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass`, while Hilbert.S5 corresponds to `ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass`. The inclusion of KTB within S5 can be understood by examining the frame properties of these classes.

Given a frame `F` that belongs to `ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass`, which includes both reflexivity and Euclidean properties, we can infer that any theorem valid in such a frame is also valid in a frame that satisfies the weaker conditions of `ReflexiveSymmetricFrameClass`. This is because `ReflexiveEuclideanFrameClass` encompasses a broader set of frame properties, rendering the theorems of KTB directly applicable within S5.

Thus, by satisfying the frame properties of `ReflexiveEuclidean`, which inherently supports the axioms and rules of KTB, we conclude that every theorem provable in Hilbert.KTB is also provable in Hilbert.S5, thereby establishing that Hilbert.KTB is weaker than Hilbert.S5.
